calls.reason: Hedged inference on mixed evidence: Zoom's filing links AI use to higher hosting costs, but Zoom bundles AI at no extra cost and Slack's $10 add-on is one example; no representative price or cost comparison.
Kalai and Vempala (STOC 2024) and Xu et al. (Jan 2024) show hallucination arises from normal predictive learning, not defects, supporting the structural-tendency reading.
No per-interaction cost or revenue allocation was found; Atlassian bundling confirms the scenario, while Box says AI use was priced into plans. Evidence is too thin to call.

ServiceNow and Atlassian materials describe optional customization alongside planned out-of-box agents that create their own plans; nothing shows whether programming was required or what agents decided at runtime.
Salesforce reports growing Agentforce ARR and expects organic reacceleration, while a TD Cowen partner survey shows subdued adoption; neither failure nor an agent-driven turnaround is established.
Workday and Atlassian describe agents that run workflows and take write actions, which challenges 'every', but these are vendor plans with no demonstrated deployment, so no confirmed counterexample.
